title: Legends of the old town
episode: Legends & Folklore of Tallinn | A Walking Tour of Estonia's Capital 🇪🇪
description: A walk through the old town’s legends: the Old Man of Lake Ülemiste, the devil’s wedding, and Old Thomas, the soldier on the weathervane of the Town Hall, the oldest Gothic town hall in Northern Europe.

title: The tower that peeks into kitchens
episode: KIEK in de KÖK | Artillery Tower | Fortifications Museum | Tallinn
description: Kiek in de Kök, Low German for “peek into the kitchen,” is a cannon tower built in the 1470s, so tall that guards could see into kitchens below. Tunnels dug in the 1600s run beneath the bastions.

title: A sea fortress turned Soviet prison
episode: International Museum for the Victims of Communism in Patarei prison
description: Patarei, a sea fortress built under the tsars in the 1820s and 1830s, became a prison used by the Soviet secret police and, during the German occupation, by the Nazis. It closed in 2002 and is being turned into a museum.

title: Tallinn at the 1980 Olympics
episode: 1980 Tallinn Archive | Estonia in Soviet Time | Olympic Games | XIX Song Festival
description: Archive footage of Tallinn in 1980, when it hosted the sailing events of the Moscow Olympics. The city built the yachting center at Pirita, the TV tower, and the Linnahall concert hall for the games.

title: How folk songs defeated an empire
episode: How Folk Music Defeated the Soviet Union
description: A video essay on the Singing Revolution, when hundreds of thousands of Estonians gathered at the song festival grounds in 1988 to sing banned patriotic songs. Estonia regained independence in 1991 with almost no bloodshed.

title: A human chain across three countries
episode: How World News Tonight covered the Baltic Chain protest in 1989
description: ABC News coverage of the Baltic Way on August 23, 1989, when about two million people held hands in a line from Tallinn to Vilnius, more than 600 kilometers. The chain began at Toompea Castle, now the parliament.

title: The country that runs online
episode: How Estonia became one of the world’s most advanced digital societies
description: How Estonia, rebuilding after 1991, put almost all government services online, from tax returns to voting, and became home to startups like Skype. Ülemiste City, an old factory district by the airport, is now its tech campus.

title: A Soviet concert hall in a Christopher Nolan film
episode: TENET: Step into epic filming locations in Tallinn
description: The Tallinn locations used in Tenet, Christopher Nolan’s 2020 thriller, including the Linnahall, a huge concrete concert hall and ice rink by the harbor, built for the 1980 Olympics and now mostly empty.

title: The smoke sauna
description: UNESCO’s film on the smoke sauna, a chimneyless sauna heated for hours with a wood fire, a tradition kept alive in southern Estonia. Old farm saunas can be seen at the open-air museum on Tallinn’s western edge.
